```{r readdata, echo = F, include = F}
# load data set
empro <- here::here("data", "EMPRO_data_20260506.RData")
load(empro)

#make enrollment month factor 
empro_data$enrollment_month1 = factor(empro_data$enrollment_month)

#make new variable for yes/no CRPC
empro_data$crpc_per = empro_data$cohort_empro != "mHSPC"

# add variable for not matched
empro_data$not_matched = ifelse(empro_data$subject %in% not_matched, 1, 0)

#relabel new vars
var_label(empro_data) <- list(
  enrollment_month1 = "Study visit at entry")

# read in site-level data
site_data <- read.csv("H:/GU/EMPRO/Randomization/randscheme_final.csv") %>% 
  rename(site_country = Country,
         site_timetodx = timetodx,
         site_crpc = CRPC)

# reflected sqrt function
eortc_trans <- function(x){sqrt(100 - x)}
# inverse
inv_eortc_trans <- function(x){100 - x^2}
# transformation name
trans <- "√(100-x)"

# ever experienced the technical bug
bug_outcome <- triggers_long %>% 
  mutate(bug = ifelse(after_bug=="Bug present", 1, 0)) %>% 
  group_by(subject) %>% 
  summarize(n_bug = sum(bug),
            n_total = n()) %>% 
  select(subject, n_bug, n_total) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  mutate(p_bug = n_bug/n_total,
         bug_group = case_when(
           p_bug==0 ~ 1,
           p_bug>0 & p_bug<1 ~ 2,
           p_bug==1 ~ 3
         ))

# analysis data set (remove exclusions)
analysis_data <- empro_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(empro_cnstdate) & enrollment_month<=45 & !is.na(cohort_empro)) %>%
  mutate(enrollment_month1 = fct_drop(enrollment_month1)) %>%
  mutate(sitenew = case_when(
    site=="Cross Cancer Institute (Alberta Health Services)" ~ "Cross Cancer Institute",
    site=="Guys St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust" ~ "Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust",
    site=="Royal Brisbane & Women’s Hospital" ~ "Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital",
    site=="St. Vincent’s Hospital Sydney" ~ "St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney",
    site=="University of Virgina (UVA)" ~ "University of Virginia", 
    site=="Royal Brisbane & Women's Hospital" ~ "Queensland University of Technology",
    site=="NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital" ~ "Weill Cornell Medical Center",
    TRUE ~ site),
    ecog3 = replace_na(ecog2, "Unknown"),
    crpc_per = factor(crpc_per, levels=c("FALSE", "TRUE"), labels = c("mHSPC", "CRPC"))) %>% 
  left_join(site_data, by = c("sitenew"="sitegp")) %>% 
  mutate(# re-order - this matches the order from when they were randomized (must match constrained space file)
    sitenew = factor(sitenew,
                           levels = c("Queensland University of Technology",
                                      "Eastern Health",
                                      "St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney",
                                      "Macquarie University Hospital",
                                      "Cross Cancer Institute",
                                      "Ottawa Hospital Cancer Centre",
                                      "The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust",
                                      "Duke Comprehensive Cancer Center",
                                      "Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center",
                                      "Weill Cornell Medical Center",
                                      "University of Virginia")),
  # transformed EORTC
  eortc_6norm = eortc_trans(eortc_6)) %>% 
  set_variable_labels(ecog3="ECOG",
                      enrollment_month1 = "Study visit at entry", 
                      arm_c = "Arm",
                      eortc_6norm = "EORTC at 6 mo (transformed)",
                      crpc_per = "Disease state") %>% 
  # add in bug info
  full_join(bug_outcome, by="subject") %>% 
  mutate(bug_group = case_when(
    !is.na(bug_group) ~ bug_group,
    arm=="control" ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ 4),
    bug_group = factor(bug_group, 
                       levels = 0:4,
                       labels = c("Control", 
                                  "No questionnaires impacted by bug", 
                                  "Some intervention questionnaires impacted by bug", 
                                  "All intervention questionnaires impacted by bug", 
                                  "No intervention questionnaires completed")))

# complete data at 6 mo
analysis_data2 <- analysis_data %>% 
  filter(!is.na(eortc_6)) 

# patient counts
n_crpc <- analysis_data %>% filter(cohort_empro=="CRPC" & arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
n_mhspc <- analysis_data %>% filter(cohort_empro=="mHSPC" & arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()
n_intervention <- analysis_data %>% filter(arm=="intervention") %>% nrow()

```

# Permutation test

Intervention effect was analyzed using linear mixed models, with statistical inference based on permutation tests applied to model residuals. The permutations tests are complete case analysis.

## Model 1

Only adjusted for subject-level covariates

```{r}
# should be:
#                                             clustername allocation
# 1                   Queensland University of Technology          0
# 2                                        Eastern Health          1
# 3                         St. Vincent's Hospital Sydney          0
# 4                         Macquarie University Hospital          1
# 5                                Cross Cancer Institute          1
# 6                         Ottawa Hospital Cancer Centre          0
# 7                The Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust          0
# 8    Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust          0
# 9              Guys and St. Thomas NHS Foundation Trust          1
# 10 University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust          1
# 11                     Duke Comprehensive Cancer Center          0
# 12               Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center          1
# 13                         Weill Cornell Medical Center          1
# 14                               University of Virginia          0

perm1 <- cptest(outcome = analysis_data2$eortc_6norm,
       clustername = analysis_data2$sitenew,
       z = data.frame(analysis_data2[ , c("age_baseline", "ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "crpc_per")]), 
       cspacedatname = "H:/GU/EMPRO/Randomization/empro_constrained.csv",
       outcometype = "continuous",                                                      
       categorical = c("ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "crpc_per"))

```

`r perm1$pvalue_statement`

# F-test

Adjusted for subject-level covariates and site-level covariates included in the randomization scheme (measured at the time of randomization).

**Interpretation**: The outcome was transformed as √(100 − EORTC), which reverses the direction of the scale: higher EORTC values (better function) correspond to smaller transformed values, and lower EORTC values correspond to larger transformed values. As a result, the direction of associations in the mixed model is inverted:

-   Covariates associated with worse EORTC scores on the original scale will have positive coefficients on the transformed scale.

-   Covariates associated with better EORTC scores will have negative coefficients on the transformed scale.

This sign change reflects the monotonic decreasing nature of the transformation rather than a substantive reversal of the underlying relationships.

## Complete case analysis

### Model results

```{r}
# linear mixed model
fit_adj <- lmer(eortc_6norm ~ arm_c + age_baseline + ecog3 + race_gp + educ_gp + crpc_per + 
              site_country + site_timetodx + site_crpc +
              (1 | sitenew), data = analysis_data2, REML = TRUE)
# singular warning: random-effect variance for sitenew is estimated ≈ 0 in many imputations.

# main table with term p-values
main_tab <- fit_adj %>% 
  tbl_regression(label = list(arm_c = "Arm", 
                              ecog3 = "ECOG", 
                              site_country = "Country", 
                              site_timetodx = "Time from diagnosis to enrollment (site average)", 
                              site_crpc = "Percent CRPC (site average)")) %>% 
  bold_labels() 

# table of only global p-values
global_p_tab <- fit_adj %>% 
  tbl_regression(label = list(arm_c = "Arm", 
                              ecog3 = "ECOG", 
                              site_country = "Country", 
                              site_timetodx = "Time from diagnosis to enrollment (site average)", 
                              site_crpc = "Percent CRPC (site average)")) %>% 
  add_global_p() %>% 
  bold_labels() %>% # show_header_names()
  modify_column_hide(estimate) %>% 
  modify_column_hide(conf.low)

# merge tables
cc_tab <- tbl_merge(list(main_tab, global_p_tab)) %>% 
  modify_spanning_header(everything() ~ NA_character_) %>% 
  modify_header(p.value_1 ~ "**P-value**",
                p.value_2 ~ "**Global p-value**")



# hide wrong p-value for each variable
cc_tab |>
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        # Remove term p-values for variables that use global tests
        p.value_1 = if_else(
          variable %in% c("ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "site_country"),
          NA,
          p.value_1
        ),
        # Remove global p-values for variables that use term-level tests
        p.value_2 = if_else(
          variable %in% c("arm_c", "crpc_per", "site_timetodx", "site_crpc", "age_baseline"),
          NA,
          p.value_2
        )
      )
  ) %>% 
  modify_footnote(
    p.value_2 ~
      "Global p-values obtained from ANOVA"
  ) 


```

### Estimated marginal means

Estimated marginal means, back-transformed to the original EORTC scale.

```{r}
# estimated marginal means by arm
emm_arm <- emmeans(fit_adj, ~ arm_c)

# convert to data frame and back-transform
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_arm) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_orig = inv_eortc_trans(emmean),
    lower_orig = inv_eortc_trans(upper.CL),
    upper_orig = inv_eortc_trans(lower.CL)
  ) %>%
  select(
    arm_c,
    mean_orig,
    lower_orig,
    upper_orig
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_orig = round(mean_orig, 1),
    lower_orig = round(lower_orig, 1),
    upper_orig = round(upper_orig, 1)
  )

# create table
gt(emm_df) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Adjusted Mean Composite Scores by Treatment Arm",
    subtitle = paste0("Back-transformed estimates from the ", trans, " scale"),
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    arm_c = "Treatment Arm",
    mean_orig = "Adjusted Mean",
    lower_orig = "Lower 95% CI",
    upper_orig = "Upper 95% CI"
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "Means were estimated from the mixed model and",
      "back-transformed to the original composite score scale."
    )
  )


```

### Model diagnostics

These plots show normality of the residuals from the mixed model, which further supports the transformation of the outcome, EORTC.

```{r, fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
# residuals
resid <- resid(fit_adj)        # conditional residuals
fitted <- fitted(fit_adj)

plot(fitted, resid,
     xlab = "Fitted values",
     ylab = "Residuals")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

hist(resid, breaks = 30, main = "Residuals", xlab = "Residual value")

qqnorm(resid)
qqline(resid)

```

## Missing at random (MAR)

The first imputation analysis assumes that data are missing at random. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation with predictive mean matching (100 imputations). Linear mixed models with a random intercept for site were fitted within each imputed dataset and pooled using Rubin’s rules. The outcome was analyzed on the transformed scale. Global p‑values for categorical predictors were obtained using ANOVA (F-test). Adjusted marginal means were back‑transformed to the original scale for interpretability.

### Model results

```{r, results="hide", eval=TRUE}
# impute on transformed scale

# narrow down dataset to only needed variables
to_impute_mar <- analysis_data %>% 
  select(subject, eortc_6norm, age_baseline, arm_c, ecog3, race_gp, educ_gp, crpc_per, site_country, site_timetodx, site_crpc, sitenew)

# --- Multiple imputation
imp_mar <- mice(to_impute_mar, 
            m = 100, 
            maxit = 10, 
            seed = 123, 
            method = c(subject = "", age_baseline="", eortc_6norm="pmm", ecog3="", 
                       arm_c="", race_gp="", educ_gp="", crpc_per="", sitenew="",
                       site_country="", site_timetodx="", site_crpc=""))
# - pmm: Predictive mean matching (numeric)
# - norm: Bayesian linear regression (numeric)
# - logreg: Logistic regression (factor, 2 categories)
# - polyreg: Polytomous (unordered) regression (factor, >= 2 categories)
```

Model coefficients and confidence intervals were pooled across imputations using Rubin’s rules. Global p‑values for categorical variables with \>2 levels were obtained using ANOVA, which combines information across imputations while accounting for correlations among category levels.

```{r, results="hide"}
# apply function to imputed data
fit_list_mar <- with(imp_mar, 
                 lmerTest::lmer(eortc_6norm ~ arm_c + age_baseline + ecog3 + race_gp + 
                              educ_gp + crpc_per + site_country + site_timetodx + 
                              site_crpc + (1|sitenew), REML = FALSE))

# categorical variables (all)
cat_vars <- c("arm_c", "ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "crpc_per", "site_country", "site_crpc")

# function to extract global p-value for one variable at a time
# note: this computes anova statistic in each imputed dataset and pools these statistics using a multivariate MI combination rule to produce a single p-value (MI extension of Rubin's framework for joint hypotheses)
get_global_anova <- function(mids_obj, outcome, var) {
  formula_str <- paste(outcome, "~", var)
  miceadds::mi.anova(
    mids_obj,
    formula = formula_str,
    type = 2
  ) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("variable") %>%
    filter(variable != "Residual") %>%
    mutate(
      variable = str_trim(variable),
      row_type = "label",
      p.value = anova.table.Pr..F.
    ) %>%
    select(variable, row_type, p.value)
}

# compute each p-value
global_pvals <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    cat_vars,
    function(v) get_global_anova(
      mids_obj = imp_mar,
      outcome  = "eortc_6norm",
      var      = v
    )
  )
)
```

```{r}
# output table
mar_tab <- imp_mar %>% 
  with(lmerTest::lme4::lmer(eortc_6norm ~ arm_c + age_baseline + ecog3 + race_gp + 
                    educ_gp + crpc_per + site_country + site_timetodx + 
                              site_crpc + (1|sitenew),
                  REML = FALSE)) %>% 
  tbl_regression(label = list(
    arm_c     = "Treatment Arm",
    age_baseline = "Age",
    ecog3     = "ECOG Performance Status",
    race_gp   = "Race",
    educ_gp   = "Education Level",
    crpc_per  = "Disease State",
    site_timetodx = "Time from Diagnosis to Enrollment (Site-Level)",
    site_crpc = "CRPC (Site-Level)",
    site_country = "Country")) %>%
  # add global p-value
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x %>%
      rename(original.p = p.value) %>%
      mutate(original.p = scales::pvalue(original.p)) %>% 
      left_join(
        global_pvals,
        by = c("variable", "row_type"))) %>% 
  modify_header(original.p ~ "**P-value**",
                p.value ~ "**Global p-value**") %>%
  bold_labels() %>%
  modify_footnote(
    all_stat_cols() ~

  ) %>%
```

## Missing not at random (MNAR)

Based on the relationship between ECOG and missingness of EORTC scores, we hypothesize that data are not missing at random. To try to more accurately impute data we use the following steps:

-   Participants who were deceased prior to the 6-month EORTC were assigned an EORTC score of 0.

-   Imputation for missing EORTC scores for participants alive at 6 months was done according to the methods from Carerras ACTION study method: <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12874-020-01180-y> <br>

A shift of 5–10 points was considered a small clinically important difference in EORTC, while shifts of 10–20 points were considered moderate. Accordingly, imputed EORTC scores were shifted by 0 points for ECOG 0, down by approximately 7 points for ECOG 1, down by approximately 12 points for ECOG 2–4, and down by 10 points for participants missing ECOG. This reflects increasing assumed deterioration in unobserved quality-of-life outcomes with worsening performance status.

### Deterministic

A controlled imputation approach was used in which imputed outcomes were shifted by pre‑specified ECOG‑dependent deltas. The shift was applied deterministically to all imputed values, representing the expected difference under an MNAR assumption.

#### Model results

```{r, results="hide"}

# impute on transformed scale

# The paper is implementing a pattern‑mixture / reference‑based multiple imputation approach, where:
# * You impute missing outcomes under MAR
# * Then apply a clinically motivated shift (δ‑adjustment) based on a QoL variable (ECOG)
# * The shift reflects poorer outcomes for worse ECOG categories
# This is sometimes called controlled imputation.

# Conceptual Mapping to mice
# In mice, this is implemented by:
# 1) Imputing the outcome under MAR (standard regression imputation)
# 2) Post‑processing the imputed values using:
#   * ECOG score
#   * A prespecified shift (δ) per ECOG level

# create subset of needed variables
to_impute_mnar <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(eortc_6norm = ifelse(dead6==1 & is.na(eortc_6norm), eortc_trans(0), eortc_6norm)) %>% 
  select(subject, eortc_6norm, arm_c, age_baseline, ecog3, race_gp, educ_gp, crpc_per, 
         sitenew, site_country, site_timetodx, site_crpc)


# mild option: 0, -5, -10 
# upper option: 0, -10, -20

# # set up mice
# ini <- mice(to_impute_mnar, maxit = 0)
# pred <- ini$predictorMatrix
# 
# # define a post adjustment function
# # deterministic delta‑adjustment- fixed shift for each ECOG level
# post <- ini$post
# post["eortc_6norm"] <- "imp[[j]][, i] <- imp[[j]][, i] + delta_ecog[as.character(data$ecog3[i])]"


ini <- mice(to_impute_mnar, maxit = 0)
pred <- ini$predictorMatrix
post <- ini$post


post["eortc_6norm"] <- "
    delta_ecog <- c(
      `0` = 0,   # 0: reference
      `1` = -7, # -7: small change
      `2-4` = -12, # -12: small/medium change
      `Unknown` = -10 # -10
      )
      
    # imputed value is on sqrt(100 - x) scale
    z <- imp[[j]][, i]
    
    # back-transform to original scale
    x <- 100 - z^2

    # lookup ECOG-specific original-scale delta
    d <- delta_ecog[as.character(data$ecog3[i])]
    
    # compute equivalent shift on sqrt scale
    delta_z <- sqrt(100 - (x + d)) - sqrt(100 - x)

    # apply equivalent shift on sqrt
    imp[[j]][, i] <- z + delta_z
"

# run mice
imp_mnar1 <- mice(
  to_impute_mnar,
  m = 100, 
  maxit = 10, 
  seed = 123, 
  method = c(subject = "", eortc_6norm="pmm", ecog3="", arm_c="", age_baseline="",
             race_gp="", educ_gp="", crpc_per="", sitenew="",
             site_country="", site_timetodx="", site_crpc=""),
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  post = post
)
```

```{r, results="hide"}
                                    site_timetodx + site_crpc + (1|sitenew),
```

#### Estimated marginal means

```{r}

# pooled marginal means 
# Extract fitted models
fits <- fit_list_mnar1$analyses

# Compute emmeans for each imputation
emm_list <- lapply(fits, emmeans, ~ arm_c)

# summarize emms within each imputation
emm_sum <- lapply(emm_list, summary)

# Pool estimates using Rubin's rules
Q <- lapply(emm_sum, function(x) x$emmean)   # estimates
U <- lapply(emm_sum, function(x) x$SE^2)     # variances
mi <- MIcombine(Q, U)

# Compute pooled SEs and 95% CIs (on transformed scale)
alpha <- 0.05
z <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
pooled_est <- mi$coefficients
pooled_se  <- sqrt(diag(mi$variance))
upper_CL <- pooled_est - z * pooled_se
lower_CL <- pooled_est + z * pooled_se

# create data frame
emm_imp <- data.frame(
  arm_c    = emm_sum[[1]]$arm_c,
  emmean   = pooled_est,
  SE       = pooled_se,
  lower.CL = lower_CL,
  upper.CL = upper_CL
)

# convert to data frame and back-transform
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_imp) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    mean_orig  = inv_eortc_trans(emmean),
    lower_orig = inv_eortc_trans(lower.CL),
    upper_orig = inv_eortc_trans(upper.CL)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    arm_c,
    mean_orig,
    lower_orig,
    upper_orig
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 1)))

# create marginal means table
gt(emm_df) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Adjusted Marginal Means by Treatment Arm",
    subtitle = "Back-transformed to the original composite score scale"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    arm_c = "Treatment Arm",
    mean_orig = "Adjusted Mean",
    lower_orig = "Lower 95% CI",
    upper_orig = "Upper 95% CI"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "Marginal means were estimated from pooled mixed models",
      paste0("and back-transformed from the ", trans, " scale."),
      "Inference was conducted on the transformed scale."
    )
  )
```

### Probabilistic

As a sensitivity analysis, a controlled multiple imputation approach was used in which imputed EORTC scores were adjusted to reflect departures from the missing‑at‑random assumption. Conditional on ECOG performance status, a pre‑specified downward shift was applied to imputed outcomes with a fixed probability. This probabilistic implementation allows heterogeneity in the magnitude of the MNAR departure while preserving the expected shift within each ECOG category. Shift with probability p: only shift 50% of the time, conditional on ECOG.

#### Model results

```{r, results="hide"}
# impute on transformed scale

# The paper is implementing a pattern‑mixture / reference‑based multiple imputation approach, where:
# * You impute missing outcomes under MAR
# * Then apply a clinically motivated shift (δ‑adjustment) based on a QoL variable (ECOG)
# * The shift reflects poorer outcomes for worse ECOG categories
# This is sometimes called controlled imputation.

# Conceptual Mapping to mice
# In mice, this is implemented by:
# 1) Imputing the outcome under MAR (standard regression imputation)
# 2) Post‑processing the imputed values using:
#   * ECOG score
#   * A prespecified shift (δ) per ECOG level

# set up mice
ini <- mice(to_impute_mnar, maxit = 0)
pred <- ini$predictorMatrix

# # define a post adjustment function
# # probabilistic shifting
# post <- ini$post
# post["eortc_6norm"] <- "
# delta_ecog <- c(
#   `0` = 0,   # 0: reference
#   `1` = -0.46, # -7: small change
#   `2-4` = -0.74, # -12: small/medium change
#   `Unknown` = -0.63 # -10
# )
#   p_shift <- 0.5
# 
#   shift_indicator <- rbinom(length(i), size = 1, prob = p_shift)
#   imp[[j]][, i] <- imp[[j]][, i] +
#     shift_indicator * delta_ecog[as.character(data$ecog3[i])]"

post["eortc_6norm"] <- "
  delta_ecog <- c(
    `0` = 0,
    `1` = -7,
    `2-4` = -12,
    `Unknown` = -10
  )

  p_shift <- 0.5

  # MNAR indicator
  shift_indicator <- rbinom(length(i), size = 1, prob = p_shift)

  # imputed values on sqrt(100 - x) scale
  z <- imp[[j]][, i]

  # back-transform to original scale
  x <- 100 - z^2

  # ECOG-specific delta (original scale)
  d <- delta_ecog[as.character(data$ecog3[i])]

  # compute equivalent shift on sqrt scale
  delta_z <- sqrt(100 - (x + d)) - sqrt(100 - x)

  # apply probabilistic shift
  imp[[j]][, i] <- z + shift_indicator * delta_z
"

# another option: add random noise around the delta
# aligns with distributional interpretation in the paper
# post["eortc_6norm"] <- "
# delta_ecog <- c(
# delta_ecog <- c(
#   `0` = 0,   # 0: reference
#   `1` = -7, # -7: small change
#   `2-4` = -12, # -12: small/medium change
#   `Unknown` = -10 # -10
# )  sigma_delta <- 1.5
# 
#   imp[[j]][, i] <- imp[[j]][, i] +
#     rnorm(length(i),
#           mean = delta_ecog[as.character(data$ecog3[i])],
#           sd   = sigma_delta)
# "

# run mice
imp_mnar2 <- mice(
  to_impute_mnar,
  m = 100, 
  maxit = 10, 
  seed = 123, 
  method = c(subject = "", age_baseline = "", eortc_6norm="pmm", ecog3="", arm_c="", 
             race_gp="", educ_gp="", crpc_per="", sitenew="",
             site_country="", site_timetodx="", site_crpc=""),
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  post = post
)
```

## Compare distributions of EORTC

These plots show the distributions of outcomes for the various models, including the complete cases and the data generated for each imputation method. Note that the values are on the transformed scale, so upward shifts in the distribution on the transformed scale correspond to lower values of EORTC on the native scale.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# complete cases
complete_cases <- analysis_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(eortc_6norm)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "Complete case")

# extract MAR-imputed values - 60 missing EORTC-6 * 100 imputations
long_mar <- complete(imp_mar, action = "long") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "MAR imputation") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    was_missing = is.na(to_impute_mar$eortc_6norm[match(subject, to_impute_mar$subject)])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(was_missing)

# extract MNAR-imputed values
long_mnar1 <- complete(imp_mnar1, action = "long") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "MNAR imputation - deterministic") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    was_missing = is.na(to_impute_mnar$eortc_6norm[match(subject, to_impute_mnar$subject)])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(was_missing)

# extract MNAR-imputed values
long_mnar2 <- complete(imp_mnar2, action = "long") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(source = "MNAR imputation - probabilistic") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    was_missing = is.na(to_impute_mnar$eortc_6norm[match(subject, to_impute_mnar$subject)])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(was_missing)


# combine all sources
eortc_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  complete_cases %>% dplyr::select(subject, ecog3, eortc_6norm, source),
  long_mar      %>% dplyr::select(subject, ecog3, eortc_6norm, source),
  long_mnar1    %>% dplyr::select(subject, ecog3, eortc_6norm, source),
  long_mnar2    %>% dplyr::select(subject, ecog3, eortc_6norm, source)
)

# density plot
ggplot(eortc_all, aes(x = eortc_6norm, fill = source)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of EORTC scores",
    subtitle = "Complete cases vs MAR and ECOG-adjusted imputations",
    x = "EORTC score",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=18, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),

        axis.title.y = element_text(angle=90, vjust=0.70, face="bold", size=18),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=14))

# stratify by ECOG
ggplot(eortc_all, aes(x = eortc_6norm, fill = source)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ ecog3) +
  labs(
    title = "EORTC distributions by ECOG score",
    subtitle = "Observed vs MAR vs MNAR imputations",
    x = "EORTC score (transformed scale)",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=18, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size=16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        axis.title.x = element_text(vjust=0.5,face="bold", size=16),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size=14),
        axis.title.y = element_text(angle=90, vjust=0.70, face="bold", size=18),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=14))


```

# Effect of technical bug
The effect of the EMPRO technical bug (thank you module not showing personalized self-management content) is analyzed using complete case analysis with a linear mixed model (F-test). A new exposure variable was created to represent the extent to which the technical bug affected each participant.

### Bug presence 
```{r}
analysis_data %>% 
  select(yn_eortc_6, bug_group) %>% 
  mutate(yn_eortc_6 = factor(yn_eortc_6, levels = c("FALSE", "TRUE"), labels=c("EORTC missing at 6 mo", "EORTC completed at 6 mo"))) %>% 
  set_variable_labels(bug_group = "Bug impact") %>% 
  tbl_summary(by=yn_eortc_6, percent="row") %>% 
  add_overall(last=TRUE) %>% 
  bold_labels()
```


### Model results

```{r}

# linear mixed model
fit_adj <- lmer(eortc_6norm ~ bug_group + age_baseline + ecog3 + race_gp + educ_gp + crpc_per + 
              site_country + site_timetodx + site_crpc +
              (1 | sitenew), data = analysis_data2, REML = TRUE)
# singular warning: random-effect variance for sitenew is estimated ≈ 0 in many imputations.

# main table with term p-values
main_tab <- fit_adj %>% 
  tbl_regression(label = list(bug_group = "Bug impact", 
                              ecog3 = "ECOG", 
                              site_country = "Country", 
                              site_timetodx = "Time from diagnosis to enrollment (site average)", 
                              site_crpc = "Percent CRPC (site average)")) %>% 
  bold_labels() 

# table of only global p-values
global_p_tab <- fit_adj %>% 
  tbl_regression(label = list(bug_group = "Bug impact", 
                              ecog3 = "ECOG", 
                              site_country = "Country", 
                              site_timetodx = "Time from diagnosis to enrollment (site average)", 
                              site_crpc = "Percent CRPC (site average)")) %>% 
  add_global_p() %>% 
  bold_labels() %>% # show_header_names()
  modify_column_hide(estimate) %>% 
  modify_column_hide(conf.low)

# merge tables
cc_tab <- tbl_merge(list(main_tab, global_p_tab)) %>% 
  modify_spanning_header(everything() ~ NA_character_) %>% 
  modify_header(p.value_1 ~ "**P-value**",
                p.value_2 ~ "**Global p-value**")



# hide wrong p-value for each variable
cc_tab |>
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        # Remove term p-values for variables that use global tests
        p.value_1 = if_else(
          variable %in% c("bug_group", "ecog3", "race_gp", "educ_gp", "site_country"),
          NA,
          p.value_1
        ),
        # Remove global p-values for variables that use term-level tests
        p.value_2 = if_else(
          variable %in% c("crpc_per", "site_timetodx", "site_crpc", "age_baseline"),
          NA,
          p.value_2
        )
      )
  ) %>% 
  modify_footnote(
    p.value_2 ~
      "Global p-values obtained from ANOVA"
  ) 


```

### Estimated marginal means

Estimated marginal means, back-transformed to the original EORTC scale.

```{r}
# estimated marginal means by arm
emm_arm <- emmeans(fit_adj, ~ bug_group)

# convert to data frame and back-transform
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_arm) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_orig = inv_eortc_trans(emmean),
    lower_orig = inv_eortc_trans(upper.CL),
    upper_orig = inv_eortc_trans(lower.CL)
  ) %>%
  select(
    bug_group,
    mean_orig,
    lower_orig,
    upper_orig
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    mean_orig = round(mean_orig, 1),
    lower_orig = round(lower_orig, 1),
    upper_orig = round(upper_orig, 1)
  )

# create table
gt(emm_df) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Adjusted Mean Composite Scores by Bug Impact",
    subtitle = paste0("Back-transformed estimates from the ", trans, " scale"),
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    bug_group = "Bug Impact",
    mean_orig = "Adjusted Mean",
    lower_orig = "Lower 95% CI",
    upper_orig = "Upper 95% CI"
  ) %>%
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = paste(
      "Means were estimated from the mixed model and",
      "back-transformed to the original composite score scale."
    )
  )


```


# Overall survival
Participants were censored
```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7, echo=FALSE}
survfit2(Surv(limbo, dead=="Yes") ~ arm_c, data = analysis_data) %>% 
  ggsurvfit(linewidth=2, type = "risk") +
  add_censor_mark(size = 2) +
  add_risktable(risktable_stats = c("{n.risk}"),
                size = 5,
                theme =   
                  list(
                    theme_risktable_default(axis.text.y.size = 14, 
                                            plot.title.size = 14),
                    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
                  )) +
  scale_ggsurvfit(x_scales = list(breaks = seq(0, 12, 3))) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 12.2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.15),
                     labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  # update figure labels/titles
  labs(
    y = "Cumulative incidence of death (%)",
    x = "Months from EMRPO enrollment",
    title = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

```
